'''Alexander Murray MacBeath''' (30 June 1923 [[Glasgow]] – 14 May 2014 [[Warwick]])<ref name="scotsman">{{citation|title=Obituary: Professor Murray MacBeath, mathematician and wartime codebreaker|issue=Friday 27 June |year=2014|first=Campbell|last=Thomas|url=https://www.scotsman.com/news/obituaries/obituary-professor-murray-macbeath-mathematician-and-wartime-codebreaker-1533663|journal=The Scotsman}}</ref><ref name="times">[https://www.thetimes.com/comment/register/article/professor-murray-macbeath-6hk9hvhb90t Professor Murray MacBeath], The Times, Friday 27 June 2014</ref><ref name="LMS obit">{{citation|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Obituaries/Macbeath_LMS/ |first=Bill|last=Harvey |work=LMS Newsletter|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]] |date=July 2014 |via=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]] |title=Murray Macbeath }}</ref> was a Scottish mathematician who worked on [[Riemann surface]]s. [[MacBeath surface]]s and [[MacBeath regions]] are named after him.

== Early life and education ==
MacBeath was the son of Alexander MacBeath, a philosopher and logician who took a position at [[Queen's University Belfast]] in 1925,<ref>{{citation|title=Obituary: Professor Alexander MacBeath|journal=Glasgow Herald|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=2507&dat=19641216&id=dG5AAAAAIBAJ&sjid=oKMMAAAAIBAJ&pg=6436,2594915|date=16 December 1964}}.</ref> soon after Murray was born. Murray also studied at Queen's University, earning a B.A. with honours in 1943.<ref name="scotsman"/>

During World War II, he worked in [[Hut 7]] of the [[Government Communications Headquarters#Government Code and Cypher School (GC&CS)|Government Code and Cypher School]] at [[Bletchley Park]], breaking ciphers used for military communications by the Japanese navy and, later, the army.<ref name=tutor>[https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Macbeath/ Alexander Murray Macbeath at MacTutor] [[University of St Andrews]]</ref>

He earned an M.A. (again with honours) from Clare College, Cambridge in 1948. With a Commonwealth Fund fellowship, he then attended [[Princeton University]],<ref name="scotsman"/> where he earned his Ph.D. on "The Geometry of Non-Homogeneous Lattices" in 1950 under the supervision of [[Emil Artin]].<ref>{{Mathgenealogy|id=24339}}</ref>

== Career ==
He taught at [[Keele University]] and the [[University of Dundee]] before moving to the [[University of Birmingham]] in 1963 where he stayed until 1979 as Mason Professor,<ref name="LMS obit"/> then moved back to the [[University of Pittsburgh]] in the United States until he reached their statutory retirement age of 60.<ref name="scotsman"/>

He subsequently took up a position at the [[University of Dundee]] where he remained for a number of years, before moving to Warwickshire where at the [[University of Warwick]] he held the position of emeritus professor of mathematics.

== Death ==
Professor MacBeath died on 14 May 2014 in Warwick, England.
